patch_description: The current program regressed vs. the 0.77-scoring ancestor because (a) each Metropolis step recomputes the full hull area (O(n log n) Python) inside `_score`, making annealing both slow and noisy, and (b) annealing directly on the hard minimum gets stuck in flat minima. The top prior program used a *smooth* objective (mean of the K smallest triangle areas, unnormalized during optimization, since the problem is scale-invariant and the hull barely changes during local moves) with targeted geometric moves, which is a strictly better search landscape. I restore that smooth-score annealing with targeted "push away from the opposite edge" moves, and — per the recommendation — replace the fixed ×0.88/600 step ladder with **adaptive step control**: track the acceptance rate over the last 200 proposals; if below 15% halve the step, if above 50% multiply by 1.5 (capped at 0.05). This keeps the anneal in the productive acceptance band longer. The final selection is done on the true normalized minimum (area/hull area), so the smooth surrogate only steers the search, not the reported answer. I also trim polish iterations to keep eval time near the 5s regime.
